- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to dampen.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to account for reversal bias.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.2), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- Avoid forecasting >15% above recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.8) — otherwise, risk overfitting to short-term momentum.
